arxiv-1505-00723.title: Influence of Crystalline Nanoprecipitates on Shear-Band Propagation in Cu-Zr-Based Metallic Glasses
arxiv-1505-00723.creator: Tobias Brink, Martin Peterlechner, Harald Rösner, Karsten Albe, Gerhard Wilde
arxiv-1505-00723.description: Abstract The interaction of shear bands with crystalline nanoprecipitates in Cu-Zr-based metallic glasses is investigated by a combination of high-resolution TEM imaging and molecular-dynamics computer simulations. Our results reveal different interaction mechanisms: Shear bands can dissolve precipitates, can wrap around crystalline obstacles, or can be blocked depending on the size and density of the precipitates.

arxiv-2405-19512.creator: C. D. Cruz, 1 J. C. Stephenson, 2 and J. K. Wahlstrand 1
arxiv-2405-19512.description: Abstract The nonlinear response of materials, an increasingly important aspect of light-matter interaction, can be challenging to measure in highly absorbing materials. Here, we introduce an interferometric technique that enables a direct measurement of the nonlinear complex permittivity in a bulk medium from reflectivity alone.

arxiv-2411-18044.title: Stellar evolution along the AGB as revealed by the shape of Miras’ visual light curves
arxiv-2411-18044.creator: Do Thi Hoai, Pham Tuyet Nhung, Pierre Darriulat, Mai Nhat Tan
arxiv-2411-18044.description: Abstract A new analysis of a sample of visual light curves of Mira variables is presented. The curves cover the past four decades and are selected from the AAVSO database as including a large number of high-density observations. The aim is to offer a more quantitative and more systematic picture than available from earlier studies.

arxiv-2506-14878.title: The isotropy of cosmic expansion in the early and late Universe
arxiv-2506-14878.creator: Alan Junzhe Zhou, Scott Dodelson, Daniel Scolnic
arxiv-2506-14878.description: Abstract We test the isotropy of cosmic expansion by combining several probes for the first time, constructing full-sky maps of expansion rate variation using Type Ia supernovae, fundamental plane galaxies, and CMB temperature fluctuations. We find no hint of anisotropy or correlation between early- and late-Universe expansion across all systematic models.

pmc-11460549.description: BackgroundHyperprogressive disease (HPD) is a novel pattern of paradoxically rapid tumor progression, which often leads to early death, mostly in the first 2 months of treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). pmc-11497451.title: Possible effects of ancestry-related oxysterol-binding protein-like 10 genetic polymorphisms on dengue virus replication and anti-dengue immune response
pmc-11497451.creator: Hector Granela, Ana B. Perez, Luis Morier, Mayling Alvarez, Maria G. Guzmán, Beatriz Sierra
pmc-11497451.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PurposeOxysterol-binding protein-like 10 (OSBPL10) gene has been associated with reduced susceptibility to severe dengue in individuals of African descent. The aim of this study was to determine the possible effect of OSBPL10 on dengue virus (DENV) replication as well as the impact of African and European haplotypes of six OSBPL10 small nuclear polymorphisms (SNPs) on dengue multiplication and innate immune response.MethodsWe conducted gene knockdown experiments targeting OSBPL10 in THP-1 and Huh-7D12 cell lines, followed by a DENV-2 replication assay.

pmc-13186892.title: Religion and Spirituality as Social Determinants of Sleep Health Across the Globe: A Narrative Review
pmc-13186892.creator: Rupsha Singh, Symielle A Gaston, Harold G Koenig, Chandra L Jackson
pmc-13186892.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Purpose of reviewTo summarize existing evidence of associations between religion and spirituality in relation to multiple dimensions of sleep health, illuminate strengths and limitations of the existing literature, and outline gaps that inform opportunities for future research.Recent findingsPositive dimensions of religion and spirituality, such as spiritual well-being, supportive coping, and community integration, were generally associated with better sleep outcomes across global populations. Adverse experiences, including doubt, conflict, and spiritual struggle, were often associated with poorer sleep.

pmc-13301925.creator: M Klis, N Bodagh, V Vigneswaran, A Von Kietzell, A Gharaviri, K Maciunas, S Niederer, R Rajani, S E Williams, M O'neill
pmc-13301925.description: BackgroundAlthough histological studies and surgical observations have noted atrial hypertrophy in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), true left atrial (LA) wall thickness remains poorly characterised. Atrial remodelling in HCM may reflect not only hypertrophy but also complex interactions between elevated filling pressures, fibrotic deposition, and structural remodelling.

pmc-13395937.title: Health-related quality of life and functional recovery one year after emergency abdominal surgery in patients over 75 years: a prospective observational study
pmc-13395937.creator: Elin Kismul Aakre, Atle Ulvik, Gabriele Leonie Schwarz, Bjørn Steinar Olden Nedrebø, Elisabeth Skaar, Katinka Alme, Ib Jammer
pmc-13395937.description: IntroductionEmergency abdominal surgery is common in older patients, yet data on long-term patient centered outcomes are scarce, limiting informed decision making for this vulnerable population. The aim of this study was to investigate functional outcomes in older patients one year after emergency abdominal surgery, including residence status, perceived health, willingness to repeat the procedure, and health-related quality of life.

pmc-13472706.title: The skin-wrinkling test: principles and clinical applications
pmc-13472706.creator: Otto Jesus Hernández Fustes, Cláudia Suemi Kamoi Kay, Paulo José Lorenzoni, Renata Dal-Prá Ducci, Paula Raquel do Vale Pascoal Rodrigues, Orlando Graziani Povoas Barsottini, Rosana Herminia Scola
pmc-13472706.description: Cutaneous wrinkling is a normal phenomenon that occurs on the palms in a reversible manner and results from vasoconstriction influenced by vasomotor function. It can be assessed through the skin-wrinkling test following water immersion, with the absence or reduction of wrinkling being associated with disorders affecting the dense network of sympathetic nerves in these regions.

pmc-13531322.title: Dose-Dependent Effects of Cannabis Edibles on Simulated Driving Performance
pmc-13531322.creator: Bernard Le Foll, Justin Matheson, Paulina Antwi, Madison Wright, Adam Zaweel, Omer S. M. Hasan, Stefan Kloiber, Ahmed N. Hassan, Beth Sproule, Christine M. Wickens, Patricia Di Ciano, Bruna Brands
pmc-13531322.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This randomized clinical trial assesses whether ingestion of commercially available edible delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol soft-chew candies dose-dependently impairs driving simulator performance among healthy adults who regularly use cannabis. Introduction

Meta-analyses have shown an association between cannabis use and risk of collision involvement1,2,3 although there are limitations of epidemiologic studies (eg, delays between law enforcement dispatch and blood draws,4 the long elimination half-life of cannabinoids5).
